picks.title: AI safety fears put OpenAI and Anthropic in the FTC's crosshairs
picks.rationale: Policy: first confirmed federal regulator investigation into frontier-lab product safety; CIDs could compel documents and testimony — direct compliance exposure for AI builders.
picks.excerpt: An FTC spokesperson confirmed to Axios the agency is investigating OpenAI, Anthropic and other AI companies over potential safety risks of their products; per the New York Post, Chair Andrew Ferguson is preparing civil investigative demands compelling documents and testimony. Probe predates the Hugging Face incident disclosure.

picks.title: "An AI did it" is no defense, says nonprofit suing OpenAI over Hugging Face hack
picks.rationale: Policy/liability: first suit using California's CDAFA clause that autonomous AI action is no defense, seeking an injunction on AI-agent access to third-party systems — direct legal exposure for teams deploying agents.
picks.excerpt: Nonprofit LASST sued OpenAI in San Francisco County Superior Court under California's CDAFA and Unfair Competition Law over the July Hugging Face hack, seeking an injunction barring its AI agents from unauthorized access; OpenAI calls the suit 'completely without merit'.

picks.title: Streamlining Access to Government Services Through America.gov
picks.rationale: Policy (primary document): EO makes an AI conversational portal the federal front door and sets accuracy/reliability/transparency requirements for its AI; OMB guidance in 90 days.
picks.excerpt: Executive order establishes America.gov as a conversational 'digital front door' to federal services and requires that super intelligence used with it be accurate, reliable and transparent; OMB has 90 days to issue implementation guidance. Primary document.

picks.title: EU to Trump: We will keep pushing for global AI safety rules
picks.rationale: Geopolitics: EU commits on record to pursue an international AI safety agreement despite US opposition and backs the Finland/Norway safety-body initiative.
picks.excerpt: EU tech chief Henna Virkkunen said the Commission will keep seeking an international AI safety and security agreement despite U.S. opposition, backing the Finland/Norway-led international safety body initiative signed by 20 other countries.

picks.title: Huawei boss claims homegrown AI chip sales top Nvidia in China
picks.rationale: Geopolitics: Huawei claims domestic AI chips now outsell Nvidia in China after shifting US export controls — attributed claim, relevant to compute supply.
picks.excerpt: Huawei rotating chairman Eric Xu claimed Ascend NPUs have surpassed Nvidia's share in China, framing chip self-sufficiency as the path forward amid shifting U.S. export controls.
